description: Figure 5(a) is a line plot illustrating the training loss curves for different methods as a function of training steps, specifically for models trained from scratch. The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” is linear and ranges from 0 to 140,000, with tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” is linear and spans from 2.4 to 3.4, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. Six distinct lines are plotted, each representing a different method: Vanilla (purple, solid line), StrmLLM (n=64) (blue, solid line), SepLLM (n=64) (orange, solid line), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green, solid line), SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red, solid line), and SepLLM (n=128) (light blue, solid line). All curves begin near a loss value of 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep decline in the first 20,000 iterations, followed by a more gradual decrease toward convergence. By iteration 140,000, all methods reach a loss value between approximately 2.5 and 2.6. The Vanilla method consistently maintains the lowest loss across all iterations, while StrmLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64) show similar trajectories, with SepLLM (n=128) converging slightly faster than the n=64 variants. The hybrid variants (H and H/T) show marginally higher loss than their non-hybrid counterparts at later iterations.
